extracted.intended_audience: NIH F99/K00 reviewers and grant program officers evaluating institutional resources for a trainee's application
extracted.subtask_description: Describe and justify institutional facilities, cores, and support services available to a predoctoral->postdoctoral F99/K00 trainee at USC and OHSU; demonstrate that the environment, technical resources, and mentorship will enable the proposed research and training plan.

rubrics_metrics.name: Access to USC research centers and thematic units
rubrics_metrics.description: The USC Suzanne Dworak-Peck School of Social Work is home to centers (Hamovitch Center for Science in the Human Services; Edward R. Roybal Institute on Aging; Center for Innovation and Research on Veterans & Military Families; USC Center for Artificial Intelligence in Society; Children’s Data Network; National Center for Excellence in Homeless Services’ Research Core; Center for LGBT Health Equity; California Social Welfare Archives) that provide resources, training opportunities, and collaborative relationships.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The presence of these centers situates the trainee's research in a diverse, interdisciplinary environment and provides access to domain-specific expertise, training, summer research awards, and administrative support for extramural grant development. Use these centers to justify intellectual environment and access to population-specific resources and data.

rubrics_metrics.name: IT services and secure data infrastructure
rubrics_metrics.description: The School provides dedicated research space, secure data storage facilities, state-of-the-art video conferencing, an IT network with computer stations, digital information and training labs, and a dedicated IT department that provides technical assistance and is responsible for access and security on computers, laptops, and mobile devices.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: List available hardware and software (Dell Optiplex 990 desktops, Microsoft Office Suite, SAS 9.2, NVivo, Bluejeans, camera/microphone), daily backups, and university cybersecurity/firewall protections to demonstrate the ability to access data analysis software and safeguard online communication during and beyond disruptions (e.g., COVID-19).

rubrics_metrics.name: Administrative support for research administration and compliance
rubrics_metrics.description: A research administration staff led by Certified Research Administrators provides assistance with proposal development and submission, pre-award responses and budget development, post-award project and budget management, and research compliance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Highlight access to institutional systems (Cayuse, TARA for research administration; iStar for IRB submissions; disClose for conflict disclosure; Sophia for inventions/IP) and describe how CRA-led staff assist with submissions, IRB pre-review, tracking, and compliance to support project management and transition from F to K funding stages.

rubrics_metrics.name: Data analysis and computational resources
rubrics_metrics.description: A team of biostatisticians, bioengineering statisticians, and a database manager assist with database creation, analytic approaches, sample size estimation, interim/final analyses, and manuscript reporting. Access to senior biostatisticians is available via the Southern California Statistical Support Network.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Document support from biostatisticians for analytical questions and availability of USC High Performance Computing Cluster (HPCC) with Linux clusters, >1.2 PB disk storage, tape storage, shared-head and compute nodes, and free accounts for investigators to handle large datasets and complex models.

rubrics_metrics.name: Doctoral program training environment and workshops
rubrics_metrics.description: The SSW doctoral program provides seminars and training workshops on proposal development and writing, funding opportunities and strategies, research preparation and training, research talks, and discussions, with an administrative coordinator supporting travel and stipends.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Emphasize access to targeted research workshops (e.g., USC Center for Excellence in Research) designed for early stage investigators and focused on skills needed to develop into an independent scientist, including grant planning and writing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Institute for Creative Technologies facilities and technical expertise
rubrics_metrics.description: The USC Institute for Creative Technologies is an interdisciplinary laboratory with dedicated administrative and research space, secure data storage, symposia spaces, full-time IT staff, encrypted data storage, desktop/laptop computers with required software (Microsoft Office, SPSS/SAS, Python, AcqKnowledge), and sufficient hardware (e.g., high-end graphics cards).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Describe access to their 20-participant computer lab and multiple individual testing rooms for human subjects research, and the lab's interdisciplinary expertise (computer graphics, animation, games, audio rendering, AI, NLP) which can support design of technology-delivered interventions and advanced data collection modalities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Human subjects research facilities and participant recruitment support
rubrics_metrics.description: Institute and campus facilities include single-, double-, and group-occupancy laboratories, participant computer labs, and infrastructure that allows recruitment of specialized subject populations (e.g., clinically trained subjects).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use these facilities to support feasibility of behavioral and intervention studies, and to argue for ease of access to specialized populations and controlled experimental settings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Overall scientific environment and institutional research capacity
rubrics_metrics.description: SSW and USC provide an interdisciplinary faculty, strong record of federal grants, core facilities, accredited IRB, library system (23 libraries and digital library), and a culture encouraging scientific research; USC has substantial annual research expenditures and ranks among top private universities in federally supported research.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Cite institutional metrics (>$700M research expenditures, alumni network) and interdisciplinary collaborations as evidence that the environment will enhance probability of success for the proposed project and trainee development.

rubrics_metrics.name: USC ADRC training and research resources
rubrics_metrics.description: The USC Alzheimer Disease Research Center (USC ADRC) and its Research and Education Core provide training opportunities, support, and resources on AD clinical studies, research design, pragmatic trial studies, and clinical experience in the memory disorder clinic.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Note availability of ADRC expertise for methodological training, access to longitudinal observational cohorts, intervention study frameworks, and clinical exposure relevant to ADRD research aims.

rubrics_metrics.name: OHSU institutional research capacity and alignment with trainee goals
rubrics_metrics.description: OHSU is a major academic health center with multiple schools (Medicine, Dentistry, Nursing, Public Health), substantial external funding (>$350M/year; large NIH support), expanding infrastructure (Knight Challenge, Collaborative Life Sciences Building) and partnerships to support trainee postdoctoral research.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use OHSU funding profile, inter-institutional building resources, and institutional emphasis to justify the postdoctoral environment and alignment with the trainee’s goals in technology-enabled aging research.

rubrics_metrics.name: Layton Aging & Alzheimer’s Disease Center (OADC) cores and resources
rubrics_metrics.description: The Layton Center organizes seven cores (Administrative; Clinical & Satellite; Data; Neuropathology; Outreach Recruitment & Outreach; Biomarkers; Neuroimaging) that provide well-characterized research participants, biological specimens, brain tissue, data provision and analytics to catalyze multi-disciplinary research in AD and related disorders.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explain how access to the OADC cores supports early detection research, markers of meaningful change (peripheral biomarkers, neuroimaging, in-home monitoring), neuropathology, testing novel treatments, and dissemination/education activities that benefit the trainee's research.

rubrics_metrics.name: ORCATECH life laboratory and technology translation infrastructure
rubrics_metrics.description: ORCATECH is dedicated to translating behavioral and social science advances into measures for health and well-being using pervasive computing, in-home/community embedded sensing, wireless communication, and data mining; it provides a Life Laboratory of community volunteers and functional algorithms of human activity.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Emphasize ORCATECH's leadership in developing ecologically valid, continuous, objective measurement methods and organizational infrastructure for disseminating new measurement approaches into research and practice—valuable for technology-based aging research.

rubrics_metrics.name: Availability of shared datasets and specimen repositories
rubrics_metrics.description: The Layton Center and ORCATECH commit to sharing data and specimens (clinical data; brain imaging data; activity, video, and audio data; recruitment data; biomarker and genetic specimens; pathology specimens; and derived data) from longitudinal cohorts (over 1,200 volunteers, 352 active as of Dec 2017).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Document management and contents of research repositories; availability of these data/specimens supports planned analyses, sample selection, and collaboration. Provide contact/protocol for detailed repository information as needed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Neuropathology Core laboratory facilities
rubrics_metrics.description: The Neuropathology Core includes dedicated laboratory space (3 rooms, 775 sq ft) with histology area (vented), biochemical workspace with biosafety cabinet, staff workspace, a dissecting alcove for fixed/frozen brain tissues, autopsy facilities in the Department of Pathology morgue, and dedicated tissue storage rooms.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Detail access to tissue dissection, autopsy procedures, and secure storage as evidence of capacity to support neuropathologic specimen handling and related research.

rubrics_metrics.name: Biomarkers Core laboratory capabilities and sample storage
rubrics_metrics.description: The Biomarkers Core has a 400 sq ft lab for blood/CSF collection processing; DNA extraction using NanoDrop; centrifuges, pipetters, hood space; and four -80°C alarmed freezers for long-term sample storage with rescue protocols for equipment failure.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Highlight sample processing workflows (CSF/plasma snap freezing, DNA extraction), equipment, and alarmed storage to demonstrate reliability and sample integrity for biomarker/genetic studies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Neuroimaging Core resources and advanced imaging expertise
rubrics_metrics.description: The Neuroimaging Core supports in vivo 3T MRI acquisition and analysis, access to 1.5T and 3T MRI systems, collaboration with the Advanced Imaging Research Center (AIRC), a longitudinal MRI database (>3700 MRIs from >1000 subjects), development of advanced imaging sequences/analysis approaches, 7T post-mortem imaging protocol, and access to radionuclear facilities (RRC) enabling tau-PET imaging.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the Core's longitudinal imaging data, advanced in vivo/post-mortem protocols, and emerging PET capabilities to justify imaging outcome feasibility, methodological rigor, and novel imaging biomarker development potential.
